passage:
For a school event, students researched how lunches look in different countries. They found rice meals, bread meals, soups, noodles, beans, and foods eaten by hand.
At first, some students judged unfamiliar meals as strange. The teacher asked them to study climate, farming, religion, history, and family habits.
The meals began to make sense.
A student said, "Food is like a map of life."
The event ended with a display, not a competition. No lunch was called the best.
Students learned that food carries geography and culture. What seems normal on one plate may look surprising on another, but each meal has a reason.
